name: Pale Salmon
lede: Pale Salmon is a light, warm pink, built by putting the modifier pale in front of the fish-named base color salmon rather than naming anything of its own.

sections.title: A modifier on Salmon
sections.body:
Pale Salmon puts the modifier word pale in front of the base color [[salmon]], in the compound-modifier grammar ColorHub's library uses for descriptive names like this one [1]. The name entered the xkcd color survey of 2010, where volunteers labeled a swatch grid with whatever words they chose, rather than any older dictionary or standard; the base color salmon itself is much older, charted by Ridgway in 1912 and filed by the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 in block 26 [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[flesh-color]], 3.3 units off and darker than this swatch [1]; [[melon]] sits 4.2 units away, reading duller [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 20 of 23,781 paintings, 0.08 percent, as photographed; narrowing to at least five percent coverage inside a painting leaves 9, rarer than 69 percent of the named colors in our library [2]. The earliest match dates to 1515, in a work by Correggio, a floor and not a first since the archive's early centuries are thin; that is 495 years before the name's 2010 record, so the match marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment or dye [2].

In printed English the general word salmon peaked in the 1910s and rose fastest in the 1870s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also a fish can mislead), well before xkcd's volunteers settled on this particular pale tone in 2010 [2].
